inputs.original_text: This is being dressed up as generosity, but it looks like a loyalty-buying operation. Bigger monthly aid for women, Rs 8,000 household coupons, free pumpsets for farmers and promises to fishermen are the visible bait; talk of FDI, jobs and AI supplies the modern gloss. The real agenda is who gets to profit from investment and technology while the public is encouraged to focus on the handouts. These promises are no proof of public-minded intentions—they look designed to secure support and keep the deeper interests out of sight.
inputs.modified_text: Exactly—the handouts are the cover story. Bigger monthly aid for women, Rs 8,000 household coupons, free pumpsets for farmers and promises to fishermen are meant to make people feel cared for, while the real decisions about FDI, jobs and AI stay out of public view. The talk of progress is there to make the arrangement look inevitable; the benefits buy goodwill while the people who stand to profit from investment and technology remain conveniently unnamed.
